83:1: God the Most High says: The valley in which flows the pus of the people of Hell at its bottom for those who cheat, meaning: for those who cheat people and deprive them of their rights in their measures or balances, less than what is due them in fulfillment. The origin of that is from something small, which is little and insignificant. The one who cheats is the one who reduces the right of the one who has the right to what is due him in fulfillment and completion in measure or weight. From this it is said of the people who are equal in calculation or number: they are equal like the shortfall of the sa`, meaning by that: like the full part of it is less than full. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: A man said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, the people of Medina give full measure. He said: What prevents them from giving full measure when God said: Woe to those who give short measure until he reached: On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, they were among the worst people in terms of measure. So God revealed: ‘Woe to those who give short measure’. So take good measure.” Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salim bin Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Qassam al-Sayrafi, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: I bear witness that every measurer and weigher will be in Hell. He was asked about that, and he said: There is not one of them who weighs as he is weighed, nor measures as he is measured, and God said: Woe to those who give short measure.
83:2: And His statement: Those who, when they take a measure from people, take it in full. God Almighty says: Those who, when they take a measure from people, take a full measure from them. And upon and from in this context alternate, except that if it is said: I took a measure from you, what is meant is: I took it in full from you.
83:3: And his saying: And if they measure or weigh for them means: And if they measure for people or weigh for them, and it is from the language of the people of Hijaz that they say: I weighed for you your right, and I weighed for you your food, meaning: I weighed for you and I weighed for you, and from the direction of the speech to this meaning, he made the pause at hum, and made hum in the accusative case, and Isa bin Omar, according to what was reported from him, made them two letters, and paused at kalawa, and at waznawa, then he began: they lose, so from the direction of the speech to this meaning, he made hum in the nominative case, and made kalawa and waznawa sufficient by themselves. The correct view in this regard is to stop at hum, because if ka-lawa and waz-waz-wa were sufficient, and hum were a new statement, then writing ka-lawa and waz-waz-wa would be with an alif separating it from hum with each one of them, since that is how the writing proceeds in similar cases, if nothing of the metaphors of the object is connected to it. So writing them in this place without an alif is the clearest evidence that his saying hum is only a metaphor for the names of the objects. So the interpretation of the statement, since the matter is as we have described, is as we have explained. His saying: They lose means: They lose them.
83:4: And His statement: Do they not think that they will be resurrected * for a tremendous Day? God Almighty says: Do these people who cheat in their measures and balances not think that they will be resurrected from their graves after their death for a tremendous Day, a tremendous matter, and a terrible horror?
83:5: God Almighty says: For a great day.
83:6: And his statement: The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. So The Day when mankind will stand is an explanation of the first day in the genitive case, but since lam was not added to it, it was returned to resurrected, so it is as if he said: Do those not think that they will be resurrected on the day when mankind will stand? It is permissible to put it in the accusative case while it has the meaning of the genitive case, because it is a pure addition, and if it were put in the genitive case in response to the first day, it would not be a mistake, but if it were raised, it would be permissible, as the poet said: I was like two men: one healthy one and the other that time had thrown away and failed He mentioned that people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds on the Day of Resurrection, until they are overcome by sweat. Some say it will be for the duration of three hundred years, and some say it will be for the duration of forty years. Who said that? Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: One of you will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: On the Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: One of them will sink into his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Humayd ibn Mas`adah told us: Yazid ibn Zurai` told us: Ibn `Aun told us, on the authority of Nafi`: Ibn `Umar said: On the Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘People will be stopped on the Day of Resurrection for the sake of God’s greatness, until the sweat will come down to the middle of their ears.’” Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds will be the Day of Resurrection because of the greatness of the Most Merciful. Then he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told me, he said: Adam told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds. He said: They will stand until the sweat reaches the middle of their ears. Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Habib told us: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: My father told us, on the authority of Salih, who said: Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This verse, ‘The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds,’ means the Day of Resurrection, until one of them will be submerged up to the middle of his ears in his sweat.” Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa bin Saeed, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: They will stand for a hundred years. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us: Yazid told us: Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds on the Day of Resurrection, until the sweat will bridle a man up to the middle of his ears. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: People will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them stands in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sulaimi, known as Ibn Sadran, told me: Yaqub ibn Ishaq told us: Abd al-Salam ibn Ajlan told us: Yazid al-Madani told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Bashir al-Ghifari: What will you do on the Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds for the duration of three hundred years of the days of this world, and no report will come to them from the heavens, and no command will be given concerning them? Bashir said: God is the one sought for help, O Messenger of God. He said: When you go to bed, seek refuge in God from the distress of the Day of Resurrection and the evil of the reckoning. Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i narrated to me, he said: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, The Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: They will remain forty years with their heads raised to the sky, no one will speak to them, and sweat will have bridled every righteous and wicked person. He said: Then a caller will call out, Is it not just from your Lord that He created you, then formed you, then provided for you, then you turned away from Him, that He should give every servant among you what he was given in this world? They said: Yes. Then he mentioned the hadith in full. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Qais bin Sakn, who said: Abdullah told us, while he was with Umar, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot and naked, bridled with sweat, and no human being will speak to them for forty years. Then he mentioned something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, he said: It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: They will stand for three hundred years. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran and Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: On the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds. He said: Ka’b used to say: They will stand for the duration of three hundred years. Qatada said: Al-Ala’ bin Ziyad Al-Adawi told us: It has reached me that on the Day of Resurrection, the believer’s prayer will be shortened until it is like one of his obligatory prayers. He said: Mahran told us, he said: Al-Amri told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: On the Day when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds. He said: A man will stand in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: People will stand before the Lord of the Worlds until one of them stands in his sweat up to the middle of his ears. Yaqoub said, Ismail said, I said to Ibn Awn: Is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned in this hadith? He said: Yes, God willing. Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us: My uncle told me: Malik bin Anas told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, until one of them will sink into his sweat up to halfway to his ears.
83:7: God Almighty says: No, meaning the matter is not as these infidels think, that they will not be resurrected or punished. Their book in which is written their deeds that they did in this world is in Sijjin, which is the seventh lowest earth. It is a verbal noun from sijn, just as it is said: a drunkard from drunkenness, and a sinner from sin. The interpreters differed on the meaning of this, and some of them said the same as we said about it. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Mughith ibn Sami: The book of the wicked is in Sijjin. He said: In the seventh earth. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Mughith ibn Sami, who said: The book of the wicked is in Sijjin. He said: The lowest earth. He said: Satan is bound with iron and chains in the lowest earth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim told me, on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Shamir ibn Atiyyah, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, he said: We were sitting with Ka’b, I, Rabi’ ibn Khaitham, Khalid ibn Arara, and a group of our companions, when Ibn Abbas came and sat beside Ka’b and said: O Ka’b, tell me about Sijjin. Ka’b said: As for Sijjin, it is the seventh lowest earth, and in it are the souls of the disbelievers under the punishment of Satan. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. He mentioned that Abdullah bin Amr used to say: It is the lowest earth, in which are the souls of the disbelievers, and their deeds are evil deeds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada in Sijjin: He said: In the lowest part of the seventh earth. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, meaning: Their deeds are in a book in the lowest earth. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God in Sijjin, he said: Their deeds in the seventh earth do not ascend. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Omar bin Ismail bin Mujalid told me: Mutraf bin Mazen, the judge of Yemen, told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Sijjin means the seventh earth. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, in Sijjin, that he said: in the lowest earth. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, he said: Qatada told us, regarding His statement, Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, he said: The seventh lowest earth. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, No indeed! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin, he said: It is said: Sijjin is the lower earth, and Sijjin is in the lowest heaven. Others said: Rather, this is the limit of Satan. Who said that? Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar, who said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka’b al-Ahbar, and Ibn Abbas said to him: Tell me about the statement of God: Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin… the verse. Ka’b said: The soul of the wicked ascends to the heavens, but the heavens refuse to accept it. It descends to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends and enters under seven earths, until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Satan. From Sijjin, a parchment is taken out from under the boundary of Satan, and it is numbered and sealed, and it is placed under the boundary of Satan with its knowledge of destruction until the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, Indeed, the book of the wicked is in Sijjin, he said: Under the punishment of Satan. Others said: It is an open pit in Hell, and they narrated a report about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated to us by Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti, who said: Masoud bin Musa bin Miskan Al-Wasiti narrated to us, who said: Nasr bin Khuzaymah Al-Wasiti narrated to us, on the authority of Shu`ayb bin Safwan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka`b Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell, but as for Sijjin, it is open. Some Arabists said: They mentioned that the prisoner is the rock that is under the ground. He said: It is seen that the prisoner is one of its attributes, because if it had a name it would not be permissible. He said: And if I said I made it permissible because I went with the rock to mean that it is the stone on which the book is, it was a face. I chose the statement that I chose regarding the meaning of his saying prisoner because: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Ibn Numayr told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, he said: Al-Munhal Ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Zadan Abu Amr, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said: Sijjin is the lowest earth. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned the soul of the wicked person, and that it ascends to the heavens. He said: They ascend with it and do not pass by a group of angels except that they say: What is this wicked soul? He said: They say: So-and-so, using the worst of the names by which he was called in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven and ask permission for him, but it is not granted to him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle (al-A’raf 7:40). Then God says: Write his record in the lowest part of the earth, in Sijjin in the lowest earth.” Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: Yahya bin Salim told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, No indeed! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin. He said: Sijjin is a rock in the seventh earth, and the record of the wicked is placed under it.
83:8: And His statement: And what will make you know what is the Sijjin? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: What will make you know, O Muhammad? What is that book? Then God Almighty explained that, saying: It is an inscribed book. What He means by inscribed is that which is written. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding a written book, he said: a written book. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And what will make you know what is the Prisoner? It is a written record. He said: Bishr wrote the numbers for them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, an inscribed book, he said: Inscribed means written.
83:9: God Almighty says: A written book.
83:10: And His saying: Woe, that Day, to the deniers. God Almighty says: Woe, that Day, to the deniers of these verses.
83:11: God Almighty says: Those who deny the Day of Judgment, meaning: those who deny the Day of Reckoning and Recompense. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Those who deny the Day of Judgment, the polytheists said they deny the Judgment, and he recited, And those who disbelieved said, ‘Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you of the Day of Judgment?’ (Saba’: 7)... to the end of the verse.
83:12: God Almighty says: None denies the Day of Judgment except every transgressor, sinful person. He transgressed against God in His words, disobeying His command, a sinful person toward his Lord. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Woe on that Day to the deniers. God said, And none denies it except every transgressor, sinner. That is, the Day of Judgment, except every transgressor, in His words, sinful toward his Lord.
83:13: God Almighty says: When Our verses are recited to him, God Almighty says: When Our arguments and proofs that We explained in Our Book that We sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are recited to him, He says, ‘Legends of the ancients,’ meaning: He says: This is what the ancients wrote down and composed of hadiths and reports.
83:14: And His statement: No, but it has covered their hearts. God Almighty says, refuting their statement: No, that is not so, but it has covered their hearts. He says: It has overcome and submerged their hearts, and sins have surrounded and covered them. It is said from this: The wine has covered his mind, so it has covered him with a rust, and that is when he is intoxicated, so it has overcome his mind. And from this is the statement of Abu Zubayd al-Ta’i: Then when he saw him, the wine became tainted and he did not see him with piety. Meaning you see him in fear, he says: He is drunk, so he does not notice. And from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: We did not see until I left and left with Rayne and Rayne with the cupbearer who spent the night with me The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, and the hadith came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Al-Qaqa’ bin Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, it is removed, but if he returns, it returns until it becomes great in his heart.’ That is the rust about which God said: ‘No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts.’” Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Sufyan ibn Isa told us: Ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of Al-Qa’qa’, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a believer commits a sin, a black spot appears on his heart. If he repents, desists, and seeks forgiveness, it will polish his heart. If he continues, it will increase until it covers his heart. That is the rust about which God said: ‘No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts.’” Ali bin Suhayl told me: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Al-Qaqa bin Hakim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When a servant commits a sin, a black spot appears on his heart. If he repents, his heart is polished, but if he increases it, it increases. This is what God says: No! Rather, what they were earning has stained their hearts. Abu Salih al-Darari Muhammad ibn Ismail told me: Tariq ibn Abd al-Aziz told me, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of al-Qaqa’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When a servant commits a sin, a spot appears on his heart. If he repents, seeks forgiveness, and desists, his heart will be polished. This is the rust that God mentioned: ‘No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts.’” Abu Salih said: This is how he said: Rustled. Another said: Scrubbed. Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me, he said: Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: And he recited, Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts. He said: Sin upon sin until his heart dies. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts, he said: Sin upon sin until the heart becomes blind and dies. Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: No! Rather, the stain has covered their hearts because of what they were earning. He said: The servant commits sins, and they surround the heart, then they rise until they cover the heart. Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said: Mujahid showed us his hand. He said: They used to see the heart in something like this, meaning the palm. So if the servant committed a sin, he would close some of it and point with his little finger like this. Then if he committed a sin, he would close another finger. Then if he committed another sin, he would close another finger, until he had closed all of his fingers. Then he would stamp it with a stamp. Mujahid said: And they used to see that as rust. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The heart is like the palm of the hand. When a sin is committed, it clenches a finger until it clenches all of its fingers. Our companions believe that it is the rust. Abu Kurayb told us again with his chain of transmission on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The heart is like the palm of the hand. When a person sins, it contracts and closes its finger. When he sins, it contracts until it is completely closed, then it is sealed. They thought that this was the rust. No! Rather, what they were earning has rusted over their hearts. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Rather, the stain has covered their hearts, he said: The sins have covered them. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Rather, the stain has covered their hearts, sins have spread over his heart until they have covered it. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, No! Rather, it has covered their hearts, meaning: it has been sealed. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts. He said: What they were earning has covered their hearts. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Ata’, No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts. He said: Their hearts have been covered and have fallen, so they are not frightened nor do they avoid each other. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Hasan: No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts. He said: It is the sin until the heart dies. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, No, but a rust has covered their hearts. He said: The rust is the seal that seals the heart like a palm, so one commits a sin and it becomes like this. Sufyan held up his little finger and then committed a sin and it became like this. Sufyan clenched his fist and it was sealed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts - evil deeds, meaning, by God, sin upon sin and sin upon sin, until his heart died and turned black. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, No! Rather, the rust has covered their hearts. He said: This is sin upon sin, until it covers the heart and turns black. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, No! Rather, their hearts are covered with rust, he said: Their sins have overcome their hearts, so no good can come to them with them. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, No! Rather, what they were earning has covered their hearts, he said: A man commits a sin, and the sin surrounds his heart, until sins cover it. Mujahed said: It is like the verse in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin encompasses him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. (al-Baqarah 2:81)
83:15: God Almighty says: The matter is not as these deniers of the Day of Judgment say, that they will have access to God. On that Day, they will be veiled from their Lord, and they will not see Him, nor will they see anything of His honor reaching them. The commentators differed on the meaning of His statement, On that Day they will be veiled from their Lord. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: They will be veiled from His honor. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Qatada: No indeed! They will be veiled from their Lord that Day. He will not look at them, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said: Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, he said: Jarir told us, he said: Nimran Abu Al-Hasan Al-Dhamari told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah that he used to say regarding this verse, Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day, he said: The one who shows off and the one who is arrogant, who seizes people’s money falsely with his oath. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They are prevented from seeing their Lord. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Ammar al-Razi told me: Abu Muammar al-Manqari told us: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Ubayd, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding His statement, No indeed! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day. He said: The veil will be lifted and the believers will look at it every day, morning and evening, or something to that effect. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty informed us about these people that they are veiled from seeing Him. It is possible that what is meant by this is the veil from His honor, or that what is meant by it is the veil from all of that. There is no indication in the verse that indicates that what is meant by this is the veil from one meaning rather than another, and there is no report about it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that establishes its proof. So what is correct is to say: They are veiled from seeing Him and from His honor, since the report is general and does not indicate that it is specific.
83:16: And His statement: Indeed, they will enter Hellfire, God Almighty says: Then they will enter Hellfire and be roasted in it.
83:17: God Almighty says: Then it will be said, ‘This is what you used to deny.’ God Almighty says: Then it will be said to these deniers of the Day of Judgment: This torment that you are in today is the torment that you used to say you would taste in this world, but you used to deny it and reject it. So taste it now, for you have prayed to it.
83:18: God Almighty says: No indeed! The record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen. The righteous is the plural of righteous, and they are those who are righteous towards God by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. Al-Hasan used to say: They are those who do not harm anything, not even an atom. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of a sheikh, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: He was asked about the righteous, he said: Those who do not harm even an ant. Ishaq bin Zaid Al-Khattabi told us: Al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Al-Sari bin Yahya, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The righteous are those who do not harm even an ant. And his saying: In ‘Illiyyin The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of ‘Illiyyin’. Some of them said: It is the seventh heaven. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir ibn Hazim told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, he said: Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b while I was present about the highest heavens, and Ka’b said: It is the seventh heaven, and in it are the souls of the believers. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid God told us, meaning Al-Atki, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen, he said: in the highest heaven. Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen, he said: In the seventh heaven. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Aliyun, he said: the seventh heaven. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, In the highest place: in the heavens with God. Others said: Rather, the Most High is the right leg of the throne. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: No indeed! The record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen. It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: It is the right pillar of the Throne. Omar bin Ismail bin Mujalid told me: Mutraf bin Mazen, the judge of Yemen, told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyyun, he said: ‘Illiyyun’ is the right pillar of the Throne. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: In the highest heavens means: above the seventh heaven, at the right foot of the Throne. Ibn Hamid narrated: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shamir, on the authority of Atiyyah, who said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka’b al-Ahbar and asked him, saying: Tell me about the statement of God, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen… the verse. Ka’b said: When the soul of a believer is taken, it ascends with him, and the gates of heaven are opened for him, and the angels meet him with good tidings. Then they ascend with him until they reach the Throne, and a scroll is brought out for him from the Throne, and it is numbered. Then it is sealed with his knowledge of salvation through the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and the angels brought near bear witness. Others said: Rather, what is meant by the highest is Paradise. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen, he said: Paradise. Others said: At the Lote Tree of the Limit. Who said that? Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Bazuri, from the people of Kufa, told me: Ya'la ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of al-Ajlah, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: When the soul of a believing servant is taken, he is taken up to the heaven, and those brought near to God ascend with him to the second heaven. Al-Ajlah said: I said: Who are those brought near to God? He said: The one closest to the second heaven, and those brought near to God ascend with him to the third heaven, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, until he reaches the Lote Tree of the Limit. Al-Ajlah said: I said to al-Dahhak: Why is it called the Lote Tree of the Limit? He said: Because everything related to God ends there and does not go beyond it. It says: Lord of your servant so-and-so! And God knows best about him than they do. Then God sends them a sealed document that protects him from the punishment. This is the statement of God: "No indeed! The record of the righteous is in 'Illiyeen. And what will make you know what is 'Illiyeen?' It is a record inscribed, witnessed by those brought near to God." Others said: Rather, what is meant by the Most High is: in the sky with God. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, she said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen, meaning: Their deeds are in a record with God in heaven. The correct thing to say about this is that God Almighty mentioned that the book of the righteous is in ‘Illiyyun, and ‘Illiyyun’ is a plural, meaning: something above something, and height above height, and elevation after elevation. Therefore, it is made plural with the ‘ya’ and the ‘nun’, like the plural of ‘men’, if it does not have a singular or dual construction, as was reported from some Arabs by hearing: He fed us a broth of two broths, meaning cooked meat, as the poet said: I have only narrated the two Dahdahina, Qalaisat and Abkarina. He said: And our two virgins, so he pluralized it with the letter nun because he did not mean a known number of virgins, but rather he meant a number whose end is not limited, and as the other said: So the doctrines have been spread throughout the ages after the floods. Meaning: rain after rain, unlimited in number. The Arabs do the same with every plural that does not have a singular or plural, so they pluralize it for all females and males with the letter nun as we have explained. From that is their saying for men and women: twenty and thirty. So if that is like what we have mentioned, then it is clear that his saying in ‘Illiyyin means: in height and elevation, in heaven above heaven, and height above height. It is possible that that is to the seventh heaven, and to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and to the base of the Throne, and there is no report that cuts off the excuse that it means some of that and not some. The correct thing to say about this is what God Almighty said: The Book of the Righteous is ascending to a level whose end God Almighty knows, and we have no knowledge of its ultimate purpose, except that it does not fall short of the seventh heaven, due to the consensus of the hujja of the people of interpretation on this.
83:19: And His saying: And what will make you know what is ‘Aliyyun?’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, admiring Himself from ‘Aliyyun’: And what makes you know, O Muhammad, what is ‘Aliyyun?’
83:20: And His statement: A written book means that the Most High says: The book of the righteous is in ‘Illiyeen, a written book: that is, written with security from God for him from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and winning Paradise, as we mentioned before on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. And as Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, A numbered book No.
83:21: And His statement: It will be witnessed by those brought near: He says: That written book will witness the safety of God for the righteous among His servants from the Fire and their success in Paradise, the closest of His angels from each of the seven heavens. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The ones brought near will witness it, he said: All the people of heaven. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, witnessed by those brought near from the angels of God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, It will be witnessed by those brought near, that it will be witnessed by the people brought near to God in every heaven. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It is witnessed by those brought near, he said: The angels.
83:22: And His statement: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. God Almighty says: Indeed, the righteous who were righteous by fearing God and performing His obligations will be in eternal bliss that will not end on the Day of Resurrection, and that is their bliss in Paradise.
83:23: God Almighty means by His saying, On couches, they will observe: On thrones in curtains of pearls and rubies, they will observe what God has given them of honor, bliss, and joy in Paradise. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, on couches, he said: of pearls and rubies. He said: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The couches are the beds in the chambers.
83:24: And His statement: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss. God Almighty says: You will recognize in the righteous those whom God described as having the radiance of bliss, meaning its beauty, brilliance, and radiance. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement you know. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari`, recited it you know in their faces with the opening of the ta` from you know as a direct address, the freshness of bliss with the accusative of freshness. Abu Ja`far recited it you know with the damma of the ta` as a direct address, in their faces the freshness of bliss with the nominative of freshness. The correct reading for this, according to us, is what the readers of the regions do, which is to open the ta’ of ta’aruf and put the fat-ha on nadhra.
83:25: And His saying: They will be given to drink from a sealed wine means: These righteous people will be given to drink from pure wine, without any adulteration. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed wine, he said: from wine. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed nectar, meaning by nectar: wine. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed wine, he said: Wine. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Nectar means wine. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Raheeq means wine. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed wine, meaning wine. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed wine, wine is called nectar. Hassan said: They are watered with roses of geckos, and upon them is a papyrus that claps with pure nectar. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, They will be given to drink from a sealed wine, he said: It is wine. Abu Kuraib told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Nectar means wine.
83:26: As for his saying: Sealed * Its seal is musk, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is mixed and blended, its mixture and blend is musk. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Abi Ash’atha’, on the authority of Yazid ibn Mu’awiyah and Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud: His seal is musk. He said: It is not a seal, but a mixture. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Salim, on the authority of Yazid bin Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud: Its seal is musk. He said: It is not the seal that was sealed. Have you not heard one of your women say: Such and such perfume has been mixed with musk. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Abi Al-Sha’tha’, on the authority of someone who mentioned it, on the authority of Alqamah, regarding his statement, Its seal is musk, he said: Wine is sealed with musk. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah: Sealed, he said: Mixed. Its seal is musk, he said: Its taste and smell. He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Abi Ash-Sha’tha’, on the authority of Yazid bin Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Alqamah, Its seal is musk. He said: Its taste and smell are musk. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that their last drink will be sealed with musk placed in it. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, A sealed nectar, whose seal is musk, meaning wine, sealed with musk. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Its seal is musk. He said: God made wine good for them, so it was the last thing He put in it until it was sealed with musk. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Its seal is musk. He said: Its end is musk. A people for whom it is mixed with camphor and sealed with musk. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Its conclusion is musk. He said: Its end is musk. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Its seal is musk, that God made the wine good for them, and they found in it the last scent of musk. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Hatim ibn Wardan told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ibrahim and al-Hasan, regarding this verse, Its seal is musk. They said: Its end is musk. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’: Its seal is musk. So the drink is white like silver, and they seal their drinks with it. If a man from the people of this world were to put his finger in it and then take it out, there would not remain a soul except that it would find its fragrance. Others said: What he meant by the saying sealed is mud “its seal is musk” its clay is musk. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Sealed * Its seal is musk, he said: Its clay is musk. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, sealed regarding wine, its seal is musk: its seal with God is musk, and its seal today in this world is clay. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our opinion, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Its end and conclusion are musk, meaning it has a pleasant scent, and its scent is at the end of their drink, and it is sealed with the scent of musk. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings on this matter, because there is no meaning for the word seal in the speech of the Arabs except for stamping and finishing, like their saying: So-and-so completed the Qur’an, if he came to the end of it. So if there is no meaning for the word seal on the drink of the people of Paradise, it is understood that if their drink flows like water flows in rivers, and it is not aged in jugs, then it is putty on them and sealed, then it is necessary that the correct meaning is the other meaning, which is the consequence and the drink is the last, and it is what the drink is sealed with. As for the word seal in the sense of mixing, we do not know of it being heard in the speech of the Arabs. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters in the countries read it as his conclusion is musk, except for Al-Kisa’i, who used to read it as his conclusion is musk. The correct statement in our view on this matter is what the regions have read, which is his conclusion, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. The conclusion and the seal, even if they differ in wording, are close in meaning, except that the seal is a noun and the conclusion is a verbal noun, and from this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: So you stayed by my side, dying, and I started to close the door Similar to this is their saying: He is generous in nature and character. And His statement, And for that let the competitors compete, the Most High says: And for this bliss which He, the Most High, described as having given to these righteous people on the Day of Resurrection, let the competitors compete. And competition is that a man desires something from another man which he will have, and wishes that he had it without him. And it is taken from the precious thing, which is what people’s souls are eager for, and seek and desire. And it is as if its meaning in that is: let people strive for it, and for it let them race in seeking it, and let their souls be eager for it.
83:27: God Almighty says: And the mixture of this nectar is from Tasneem, and Tasneem is the activation from the saying of the speaker: The spring made them tasneem, meaning that you made it flow over them from above, so its meaning in this place is: And its mixture is from water that descends upon them from above them and descends upon them, and Mujahid and Al-Kalbi used to say the same about that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Tasneem, he said: Tasneem means to rise. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Kalbi, regarding His statement, Tasnim, he said: Tasnim is poured down upon them from above, and it is the drink of those brought near. As for the rest of the interpreters, they said: It is a spring in which nectar is mixed for the companions of the right hand and the mother of those brought near, so they drink it pure. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement, From Tasnim, he said: It is a spring in Paradise that those brought near will drink from, and it will be mixed with the companions of the right hand. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, And its mixture is of Tasnim. He said: Those who are close to God drink it pure and it is mixed for the companions. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Malik ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Masruq, and its mixture is of Tasnim. He said: A spring in Paradise that those brought near will drink pure, and it will be mixed for the companions of the right hand.
83:28: He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, A spring from which those brought near will drink. He said: Those brought near will drink pure from it, and it will be mixed for the companions of the right hand. Talha bin Yahya Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, regarding his statement, and its mixture is of Tasnim, he said: In Paradise there is a spring from which the close ones drink pure water, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink, pure water, and it is mixed with it for those below them. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Malik bin Al-Harith, regarding his statement, and its water is mixed with Tasnim, he said: Tasnim is a spring in Paradise that the close ones drink pure, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Abbas, regarding his statement, and its mixture is of Tasnim, he said: A spring from which those brought near drink, and in which it is mixed for those below them. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And its mixture is of Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink, a spring of the water of Paradise, with which wine is mixed. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And its mixture is of Tasnim, he said: Secrets that God has hidden for the people of Paradise. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Imran ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, and its mixture is of Tasnim, he said: It is the most noble drink in Paradise. It is pure for those brought near, and it is mixed for the people of Paradise. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, and its mixture is of Tasnim is a noble drink, a spring in Paradise that those brought near will drink pure, and it will be mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, From Tasnim, a spring from which those brought near drink, he said: We have been informed that it is a spring that flows from beneath the Throne, and it is the mixture of this wine: meaning the mixture of nectar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, from Tasnim, that there is a drink called Tasnim, and it is one of the most noble drinks. The interpretation of the statement is: And the nectar is mixed from a spring that rises above them, so it is poured out upon them. Those brought near to God drink from it purely, and it is mixed for the people of Paradise. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for placing the word aynā in the accusative case. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: If you wish, you can place the accusative case on the basis of they water a spring, and if you wish, you can make it a praise, so that it is cut off from the beginning of the sentence, as if you were saying: I mean a spring. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The accusative case of the ‘ayn is in two ways: One of them is that he intends min tasnim to mean a spring, so if he adds a nun, it is in the accusative case, as he said: Or feeding on a day of famine * An orphan (al-Balad 90:14-15), and as he said: Have We not made the earth a receptacle * For living things? (al-Mursalat 77:25-26). The other way is that he intends min ma’ tasnim to mean a spring, as you say: He raised a spring from which to drink. He said: If tasnim is not a name for the water, then the ‘ayn is indefinite, and tasnim is definite. If it is a name for the water, then the ‘ayn is indefinite, so it is in the accusative case. Another of the Basrans said: min tasnim is definite, then he said ‘ayn and it came out in the accusative case as an attribute of it. Another said: It is in the accusative case with the meaning: from the water that tasnim is a spring. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that Tasnim is a definite noun, and Ayn is indefinite, so it was placed in the accusative case because it was an attribute of it. We said: This is correct, because of what we have presented from the narration from the people of interpretation, that tasnim is the eye, so it was known from this that since the eye was in the accusative case and was indefinite, tasnim was definite.
83:29: And His statement: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. God Almighty says: Indeed, those who committed sins and disbelieved in God in this world were among those who acknowledged the Oneness of God and believed in Him, laughing at them in mockery. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed, in this world, saying: By God, these are liars, and they are not upon anything, mocking them.
83:30: God Almighty says: And these criminals, when those who believed passed by them, would wink at each other. He says: It was as if some of them were winking at each other about the believer, mocking and ridiculing him.
83:31: And His saying: And when they return to their families, they return in joy means: And when these criminals returned to their families from their gatherings, they returned in joy and contentment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas They turned back in joy, he said: Admiring. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement And when they return to their families, they return in joy, he said: He returned in comfort, he said: This is in this world, then the Fire will follow in the Hereafter. Some scholars of Arabic language differentiated between the meaning of fakihin and fakihin, saying: The meaning of ‘fakihin’ is ‘soft’ and fakihin’ is ‘cheerful’. Others said: They have one meaning, and are like ‘ta’im’ and ‘ta’mah’, and ‘bakhil’ and ‘bakhil’.
83:32: And His statement: And when they see them, they say, ‘Indeed, these are the ones who have gone astray.’ God Almighty says: And when the criminals see the believers, they say to them, Indeed, these are the ones who have gone astray, from the path of truth and the straight path.
83:33: God Almighty says: And they were not sent over them as guardians. God Almighty says: And these infidels who say to the believers that these are indeed astray were not sent as guardians over their deeds. He says: They were only charged with belief in God and working to obey Him, and they were not appointed guardians over others to guard their deeds and inspect them.
83:34: God Almighty says: So today - that is the Day of Resurrection those who believed in God in this world from the disbelievers therein laughing * on couches, observing - that is: on their couches in the chambers, observing them, and he is in Paradise, and the disbelievers are in Hell being tormented. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding His statement, So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, on couches, observing. He said: He meant the raised couches over which are curtains. Ibn `Abbas used to say: The couch between Paradise and Hell will have doors opened for them, so the believers will look at the people of Paradise, and the believers will be on the couches observing how they will be punished, and they will laugh at them. That will be something that God will make their eyes content with, how God will take revenge on them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, So today those who believe laugh at the disbelievers. It was mentioned to us that Ka’b used to say: There are windows between Paradise and Hell, so if a believer wanted to look at an enemy he had in this world, he would look out of one of the windows. God Almighty said, So he looked out and saw him in the midst of Hellfire. (al-Saffat 37:55), meaning in the middle of Hell. And it was mentioned to us that he saw the skulls of the people boiling. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ka’b said: There are windows between the people of Paradise and the people of Hell. No man from the people of Paradise wishes to look at another from the people of Hell except that he does so. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, lying on couches, observing. Ibn Abbas used to say: The wall is between the people of Paradise and Hell, and the doors of Paradise will be opened for the people of Paradise, and they will look while they are on couches at the people of Hell, how they are being tormented, and they will laugh at them, and that will be one of the things that God will comfort their eyes with, that they will look at their enemy, how God will take revenge on them. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers. He said: The disbelievers will be brought so that they will look at the people of Paradise in Paradise, on couches. When they look at them, the doors will be closed behind them, and the people of Paradise will laugh at them. This is what He said, So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, on couches, observing.
83:35: God Almighty says: Reclining on couches, observing.
83:36: And His statement: Will the disbelievers be rewarded for what they used to do? God Almighty says: Will the disbelievers be rewarded and given the same reward for what they used to do to the believers in this world, mocking them and laughing at them, with the laughter of the believers at them in the Hereafter, while the believers are on couches watching, while they are being tormented in the Fire. Thawb is a verb derived from the verb to reward and to recompense. It is said: So-and-so rewarded so-and-so for his deed, and rewarded him for it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Is the garment of the disbelievers what they used to do? He said: It happened. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan: Is the garment of the infidels what they used to do? when they used to mock.
